en.title: The Gentlemen Season 2 Officially Expands Its Empire of Excess
en.summary: Guy Ritchie's stylish crime saga returns with Eddie and Susie taking their weed empire global. Get ready for more mayhem, high stakes, and complicated relationships as the series unveils its second season.
en.body:
The opulent world of **Guy Ritchie's The Gentlemen** is back, and it’s bigger than ever. Season two of the Netflix hit, premiering on September 3, 2026, sees **Eddie Halstead** (**Theo James**) and **Susie Glass** (**Kaya Scodelario**) fully embracing their roles at the head of a sprawling criminal enterprise. No longer content with the confines of the Horniman estate, the duo are taking their lucrative cannabis business global, setting their sights on expansion into Italy, the Middle East, and South America.

This season picks up a year after the events of the first, with Eddie shedding any lingering reluctance to become a full-fledged crime kingpin. His journey is marked by increasing ruthlessness, leaving a trail of bodies and broken hearts as he climbs the grisly food chain. Meanwhile, his partnership with Susie, complicated by their undeniable chemistry and unspoken feelings, faces new challenges. They must navigate the treacherous landscape of international crime while managing the expectations of Susie's imprisoned, sauna-loving father, **Bobby Glass** (**Ray Winstone**), whose enterprise they now command.

The series continues to deliver the signature Ritchie blend of sharp dialogue, vivid production design, and brutal action. Expect more extravagant settings, lavish lifestyles, and the distinctive crude British slang that fans have come to love. However, the expansion of their empire comes with amplified risks, attracting new rivals and forcing Eddie and Susie into increasingly violent confrontations, including beheadings and torture scenes, as gun-toting thugs vie for control or seek to bring them down.

## The Empire Expands, The Stakes Rise

Season one was about **Eddie** coming to terms with his unexpected inheritance and the criminal empire that came with it. Season two, however, is about him *owning* it. He is no longer trying to escape the shady business; he’s actively scaling it. This shift is crucial for fans who were invested in his arc. The narrative promises to push the boundaries of this world further, as **Guy Ritchie** himself noted, “The ambition of **The Gentlemen** has accelerated, the world has expanded and the consequences carry weight.” This suggests a more complex web of alliances and betrayals, both within their operation and from external forces.

## What Fans Can Expect Next

With **The Gentlemen** officially renewed for a third season even before the second season's premiere, the future of Eddie and Susie’s empire looks secure, at least for now. The confirmation of a third season suggests that the narrative threads woven in season two will have significant repercussions. Fans can anticipate the fallout from their global expansion, the deepening of their complex relationship, and the inevitable new threats that will emerge as they continue to dominate the criminal underworld. The stage is set for even more excess, more violence, and more of the stylish mayhem that defines **The Gentlemen**.

content_raw: The Gentlemen wears its outrageousness proudly. Set in the same universe as Guy Ritchie’s middling 2019 film of the same name, season one of the adrenaline-heavy TV series made for enjoyable viewing.  In every sense of the word: This is an entertaining action romp with vivid production design and striking sets. It’s jam-packed with brutal shootouts and fiery combat that’s a lot of bloody fun and, somehow, hardly monotonous. The impeccably styled characters of its world live in lavish mansions, speak in zippy dialogue, and cherish crude British slang. Season two follows suit but broadens the show’s horizons as criminal partners Eddie Halstead (Theo James) and Susie Glass (Kaya Scodelario), who simply can’t seem to sort out their feelings for each other, strive to expand their weed empire to Italy, the Middle East, and South America. Along the way, the second season crams in violence in the form of beheadings and torture scenes, as well as gun-toting thugs who want to team up with or defeat the duo. Eddie and Susie—who run the operation for her calculating, imprisoned, sauna-loving father, Bobby (Ray Winstone)—find their command of Bobby’s enterprise challenged by rivals, loved ones, and each other. The result is a sufficiently thrilling saga that, in typical Ritchie fashion, comes with plenty of flair and ridiculous caveats. If season one was about former armyman Eddie coming to terms with his surprising Dukedom and inheritance—including a 15,000-acre estate and all the marijuana sales and distribution that came with it—then the second sees him rise to the top of a grisly food chain as he leaves dead bodies and broken hearts in his wake.  At this point, Eddie is no longer trying to get out of his dead dad’s shady business. Why would he when he’s a surprisingly conniving dude with a knack for schemes, lies, and murder? Does all the brutality take a toll on his soul? In these eight hour-long episodes, The Gentlemen finds answers to these questions that are both absurd yet quite meaningful. There’s a darkly funny church confession; Eddie’s mom, Lady Sabrina (Joely Richardson), fears he’s losing his way; and billionaire Stanley Johnston (Giancarlo Esposito) infrequently drops in to talk about Jesus and power. But this isn’t a show about contemplation—it’s not a gritty mob drama like Netflix counterparts Peaky Blinders and Ozark .  On the contrary, The Gentlemen has a revolving door of ludicrous gangsters who burst into Eddie and Susie’s lives and usually don’t exit with their own. Season two brings back some familiar faces (including an all-too-brief visit by Guz Khan as the money launderer Chucky), along with new ones who test the pair.
